title: Ferrand pushouts of a closed immersion and an integral morphism
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:Z\to T$ be $S$-morphisms, where $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Assume that for each $t\in T$ there is an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $i(j^{-1}(\{t\}))$. The pushout $P=X\amalg_ZT$ exists in the category of all schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $a:X\to P$, $b:T\to P$, and $c=ai=bj$. Its underlying space is the quotient of $|X|\amalg|T|$ identifying $i(z)$ with $j(z)$. The map $a$ is affine and integral, $b$ is a closed immersion, and the square is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its structure sheaf is
$$\mathcal O_P=a_*\mathcal O_X\times_{c_*\mathcal O_Z}b_*\mathcal O_T.$$
There is an affine open cover by $W$ such that $a^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $b^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}E$, $c^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ are affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $A\to D$ is surjective, and $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_DE)$. Here $A\times_DE=\{(a,e):a|_D=j^*e\}\subseteq A\times E$ with coordinatewise ring operations. The natural map $(X\setminus i(Z))\amalg(T\setminus j(Z))\to P\setminus c(Z)$ is an isomorphism. If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}E$ are affine, so that $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $A\to D$ surjective, then $P$ is affine: $P=\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_DE)$, with $a$ and $b$ induced by the two projections $A\times_DE\to A$ and $A\times_DE\to E$. For every open subscheme $V\subseteq P$ [def-weil-open-immersion], the inverse-image square in $Z,X,T,V$ is again a pushout of schemes. If $X$ and $T$ are separated over $S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], so is $P$. If $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $X,T,Z$ are locally of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $P$ is locally of finite type over $S$.

source.place: Tags 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), 0E26 (lemma-pushout-separated), 0E27 (lemma-pushout-finite-type); the affine case is Tag 0ET0 (lemma-basic-example-pushout). Affine charts, quotient topology, complements and open restriction are explicit in the proof of 0E25.

proof.text: Let $Q$ be the quotient of $|X|\amalg|T|$ by the equivalence relation generated by $i(z)\sim j(z)$, with the quotient topology, and write $a,b,c$ for the continuous maps. On an open $W\subseteq Q$ define $\mathcal F(W)$ to be pairs of sections on $a^{-1}W$ and $b^{-1}W$ whose restrictions to $c^{-1}W$ agree. Restrictions act componentwise. Compatible local pairs glue uniquely because each of the three structure presheaves is a sheaf, so $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of rings. This constructs the required ringed space and the formula for its structure sheaf without choosing a scheme pushout in advance.

For $t\in j(Z)$, apply [lem-sfb-integral-pinching-compatible-affines] to choose affine opens $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq T$ with $t\in V$ and $i^{-1}U=j^{-1}V=\Omega$. The common open $\Omega$ is affine and its map to $U$ corresponds to a surjection $\alpha:A\twoheadrightarrow D$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; write $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$. The subset $U\amalg V$ is saturated for the defining equivalence relation. Its image $W\subseteq Q$ is open, with inverse images exactly $U,V,\Omega$. By [lem-sfb-ring-fibre-product-spectrum], $W$ is canonically homeomorphic to $|\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_D E)|$.

Put $B=A\times_D E$. For a principal open $D(h)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$, $h=(a,e)$, its inverse images are the principal opens $D(a),D(e),D(d)$, where $d=\alpha(a)=\beta(e)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], their rings of sections are $A_a,E_e,D_d$. Thus the definition of $\mathcal F$ and [lem-sfb-ring-fibre-product-spectrum] give $\mathcal F(D(h))=A_a\times_{D_d}E_e\cong B_h$. These canonical identifications commute with restrictions. Principal opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], so the sheaf maps are inverse on a basis and hence on every open by the sheaf gluing axiom. This identifies $(W,\mathcal F|_W)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B$, including its two structure morphisms.

The subset $c(Z)$ is closed in $Q$: its inverse images are $i(Z)$ and $j(Z)$, closed because $i$ is a closed immersion and $j$ is universally closed by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]. On its complement no identifications remain, and the defining pairs of sections identify the restricted ringed space with $(X\setminus i(Z))\amalg(T\setminus j(Z))$. Cover these two open subschemes by affine opens. Their inverse images in the other component and in $Z$ are empty, hence affine spectra of the zero ring. Together with steps 2--3 this gives a cover of $Q$ by affine schemes with affine inverse images in $X,T,Z$. Consequently $(Q,\mathcal F)$ is a scheme $P$ by [def-pc-scheme]; the canonical maps $a,b$ are scheme morphisms since on every chart they are spectra of the ring projections. This proves the complement assertion and all the asserted chart descriptions.

By [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], the cover just constructed makes $a$ and $b$ affine. On each chart $B=A\times_D E$, the projection $B\to E$ is surjective: lift $\beta(e)$ along $\alpha$. Also $b$ is a closed embedding on underlying spaces: for every closed $C\subseteq T$, the inverse images of $b(C)$ in $X$ and $T$ are $i(j^{-1}C)$ and $C$, hence closed, and $b$ is injective. The map of structure sheaves is surjective locally on these charts by the surjections $B\to E$. Therefore $b$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion].

The map $E\to D$ on a chart is integral, since $\Omega=j^{-1}V$ and $j$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For $x\in A$, choose a monic equation for $\alpha(x)$ over $E$, lift its coefficients $e_r$ to pairs $(a_r,e_r)\in B$, and evaluate the lifted polynomial at $x$. Its value $u$ lies in $\ker\alpha$. Subtract $(u,0)$ from the constant coefficient in $B$; the polynomial stays monic and now vanishes at $x$. Thus $B\to A$ is integral. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-affine-cover-criterion] to the affine cover to conclude that $a:X\to P$ is integral. This is the explicit kernel calculation of Stacks Tag 0E1S, not an additional lemma being assumed.

For a chart put $I=\ker(A\to D)$. The kernel of $B\to E$ is the ideal of pairs $(u,0)$ with $u\in I$, and its extension to $A$ is $I$. Therefore $A\otimes_B E\cong A/IA=A/I\cong D$: the inverse to the quotient-tensor map sends the class of $a$ to $a\otimes1$, while $a\otimes e$ maps to $\alpha(a)\beta(e)$. The tensor relations and the surjection $B\to E$ make these maps inverse. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] this is exactly the claimed cartesian square over each $W$. These isomorphisms agree on intersections because their two projections agree; the fibre-product universal property and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] then give the global cartesian square.

For any principal open inside a chart, step 3 identifies its inverse-image diagram with the same ring fibre-product construction after localization. Localizing the surjection $A\to D$ stays surjective: a fraction $d/\alpha(a)^n$ is the image of $x/a^n$ for any lift $x$ of $d$. Hence [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout] makes this principal-open diagram a pushout in all schemes. Such principal opens form a basis of $P$. Given compatible morphisms $X\to H$ and $T\to H$ to any scheme $H$, this supplies a unique map on every basis open. On overlaps the maps coincide after restricting to any smaller basis open, by the same local uniqueness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to glue them to one map $P\to H$; uniqueness follows by restriction to the basis. Thus $P$ is the pushout in all schemes. Applying this identical basis argument only to basis opens contained in a prescribed open $V\subseteq P$ proves the open-restriction assertion, without any assertion about arbitrary base change.

If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}E$ are affine, then $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $A\to D$ is surjective by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The single-pair version of steps 2--3 identifies the whole ringed space with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_D E)$, and its maps with the two ring projections. Alternatively its unique compatible identification with the global pushout follows directly from [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout].

The map $q:X\amalg T\to P$ is surjective from the quotient description. It is universally closed: $a$ is so by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed], and $b$ is so by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]. After every base change the two component maps remain closed, and a closed subset of their disjoint union has closed image equal to the union of their two closed images. If $X,T$ are separated over $S$, so is $X\amalg T$: on the four open-and-closed components of $(X\amalg T)\times_S(X\amalg T)$ its diagonal is the two given closed diagonals and two empty subschemes. Closedness and surjectivity of its sheaf map are local on this open cover, so this diagonal is a closed immersion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated] to $q$ over $S$ (the structure map of $P$ exists by its pushout property) to obtain separatedness of $P/S$.

source.place: Tag 0E26, lemma-pushout-separated, proof, with the finite coproduct argument written out

proof.text: Assume the final finite-type hypotheses. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, refine the existing charts by principal opens contained in its inverse image; this is possible by the principal-open basis. Their inverse images remain affine principal opens by step 3. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and the resulting rings $A,E,D$ are of finite type over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. In particular finite $R$-algebra generators of $D$ also generate $D$ as an $E$-algebra. They are integral over $E$, since $E\to D$ is the chart of $j$. By [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring], $D$ is a finite $E$-module. Choose module generators $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ and lifts $x_r\in A$ along $A\twoheadrightarrow D$.

source.place: Tag 0E27, lemma-pushout-finite-type; reduction to Tag 00IT, more-algebra.tex, lemma-fibre-product-finite-type

proof.text: Set $B=A\times_D E\subseteq A\times E$. The elements $1,x_1,\ldots,x_n$ generate $A$ as a $B$-module: write $\alpha(x)=\sum\beta(e_r)d_r$, lift each $e_r$ to $(a_r,e_r)\in B$, and observe that $x-\sum a_rx_r\in I=\ker\alpha$ is the image of an element $(u,0)\in B$, hence is a $B$-multiple of $1$. The $B$-module $E$ is cyclic because $B\to E$ is onto. Thus $A\times E$ is module-finite over $B$, generated by $(1,0),(x_r,0),(0,1)$. It is a finite-type $R$-algebra: use $(1,0)$, the pairs $(a_r',0)$ from finite $R$-algebra generators of $A$, and $(0,e_s')$ from generators of $E$. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-tate-subalgebra-finite-type] to $R\to B\subseteq A\times E$ to conclude $B$ is of finite type over $R$. These charts cover $P$, so the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives that $P\to S$ is locally of finite type. This writes out the argument of Tag 00IT rather than replacing the final clause by a new node with that same clause.
